findings.title: Keep mode and effort visible when model identifiers fill the pane
findings.impact: For an accepted long model ID, the native ACP view permanently hides the following reported and requested mode/effort at ordinary terminal widths. This defeats the launch contract's visible effective-or-unreported settings, including the permission-relevant mode, even though the canonical configuration contains them.
findings.evidence: AgentView::sync at lines 287–301 concatenates model, mode and effort onto one reported line and one requested line. The new draw block at lines 972–975 uses Paragraph::new(self.settings.as_str()) without wrapping and allocates exactly three rows. Setting IDs may be 256 bytes, so, for example, a valid 100-character model ID exceeds a 120-column pane before either mode or effort is reached. History scrolling and interaction navigation do not scroll this settings paragraph. The block is added by the base patch; short fixture display checks do not cover this case.
findings.fix: Render settings using width-aware wrapping with sufficient allocated rows, or provide an explicit read-only settings detail/scroll surface. Ensure reported and requested mode/effort remain reachable for bounded long identifiers; add a native rendering regression using a long accepted model ID at an ordinary terminal width.

summary: Independent static review covered all 32 frozen files, the three settled E06 stories, the required threat model and PLAN lines 1–45. Score is 100 × 31/32 = 96.875; the source gate is FAIL because one supported Should-fix remains in native settings visibility. No additional concrete protocol, launch-authority, recovery, ownership or resource-lifecycle defect was established. This verdict is not installed-OMP or runtime acceptance.
limits: Read-only static source/diff review; no edits, builds, tests, lint, formatters, providers, source/shell execution, auth/config/daemon/global operations or commits. No prior review/audit/runtime reports, saved handoffs/execution logs or private retired fixtures were used. All frozen files were read across this review's source slices; PLAN was restricted to lines 1–45. Checklist PASS entries mean static support/no supported defect, not exercised acceptance. Genuine installed-OMP interoperability, provider/auth isolation and budgets, actual allow/deny effects, stable live identities, terminal restoration and process/endpoint/socket/root/sentinel cleanup remain separate runtime gates owned by the parent. Historical native application-settlement limitations and authorization caps remain unchanged.
